content:
Using artificial intelligence tools to generate code is becoming more and more common. This is also affecting the Lean community, as well as Mathlib and this Zulip instance. Leaving a debate about benefits and downsides aside, this poses practical challenges for moderating this instance: we want to preserve Mathlib's quality standards, and a high standard of discussion on Zulip. We also need to protect reviewers and maintainers from burnout due to dealing with too much AI slop. For all these reasons, Mathlib has an AI policy, which was already discussed within the reviewer and maintainers team (but also publicly on Zulip, e.g. here). It lays down some rules about its use. In particular,

  • if you use AI, you must disclose this in the PR description,
  • all AI-generated code must be understood and vouched for,
  • reviewers will summarily close without comment any low quality PR produced using LLMs,
  • using an LLM when writing comments on Github or Zulip is not allowed: use your own words,
  • consider if your use of AI is appropriate. When reviewing PRs, we are particularly concerned that the pedagogical value of the reviewers work is wasted if there is not a human contributor actively learning.

This policy is enforced in the same manner as the community guidelines: this can include closing or deleting slop PRs, deleting such comments and temporary suspension from Zulip.

We already know that AI is effective at formalizing mathematics. Merely asking an LLM to prove a theorem does not advance mathlib: it adds little to our understanding of formalized mathematics. You will learn far more by trying to write the code yourself. The Lean community has traditionally been friendly and welcoming. Let us preserve this human touch, even when computers can be used more in our work!
